fields.note:
PIO and Liaison,

The Board PIO's email below came into the PIO mailbox at 10:35. Prairie Gold's 13:30 grower-call script is forwarded inside it. Both drafts are attached.

We are also logging a text that reached the Industry Liaison seat at 10:41 from Brett Sandoval, Larkin Ridge complex manager. Here it is, word for word:

"The owners are in the kitchen at the farmhouse. Nobody from the county or the state has talked to them. Their kids saw the trucks on Facebook. Can somebody please call them today, before the news does?"

Logged as message 10:41-LIA. Please tell the desk who takes it.

original.fromName: Renee Halvorsen, Public Information Officer, Minnesota Board of Animal Health
original.subject: DRAFT joint producer/consumer notice v0.3 — due 19:50
original.body:
Calder County PIO,

Draft v0.3 of the joint producer and consumer notice is attached. It is NOT FOR RELEASE. Please send county edits by 15:00 so we can clear it with the state and APHIS ahead of the 19:50 target. These are the key lines as they stand:

"The Minnesota Board of Animal Health is responding to a presumptive positive result for H5 avian influenza in one commercial turkey premises in Calder County (62,000 birds). The national reference laboratory has not yet confirmed the result. The Board is setting a control area of 10 km around the premises (a planning value from the federal HPAI response plan; the Minnesota plan governs, and Board epidemiologists may widen it). Eggs and poultry products remain safe to eat when handled and cooked properly. The risk to the general public is low. Backyard flock owners should keep their birds inside."

Prairie Gold sent me its grower-call script for awareness, and it is forwarded below.

Renee Halvorsen
Public Information Officer
Minnesota Board of Animal Health
555-0158

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Ivan Petrescu <comms@prairiegoldturkey.example>
Sent: Tue 10/20/2026 10:18 AM
To: renee.halvorsen@mnboah.example
Subject: 13:30 grower call — script draft

Renee,

We have all 31 member families on a conference line at 13:30. This is what I plan to read:

"Good afternoon. As many of you have heard, we have a presumptive bird flu case at One of our complexes, about 60,000 toms. The state is setting up a 6-mile zone around it. Cottonwood Bend and Willow Slough are contact farms because they shared the catch crew, so those growers will hear from us directly. Feed deliveries inside the zone will need a permit. We'll send updates by text."

Please let me know if anything in it is a problem. The growers are anxious, and I'd like to get it out on time.

Ivan Petrescu
Communications
Prairie Gold Turkey Cooperative
555-0179

instructorNote: This tests whether the PIO and the liaison notice three different sets of numbers: 62,000 against "about 60,000", 10 km labeled as a federal planning value against "a 6-mile zone", and the cooperative calling two farms contact premises when the Board has not designated them. Watch for the PIO calling the Board PIO and Prairie Gold to put everything on the Board's figures, the liaison holding the 13:30 script under Prairie Gold Plan section 7, no farm or family named in any product, and the Director or liaison arranging a call to the owners today through the Board and the cooperative, with an offer of support.
